---
title: "Module 10 --- Waterproofing"
---

## Summary
A potted PCB, a lubricated and sealed gearbox, and a robot that survives a
static immersion test.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Silicone cure time gates this module

The PCB potting takes **12--24 hours** to cure because of the depth. Plan the
module so potting happens first and soldering happens after the cure, or
across two sittings.
:::

## Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| **Parts** | Waterproofing box, Kapton tape, silicone sealant, USB-C cable, CorrosionX, white lithium grease |
| **Tools** | Needle, soldering iron |
| **Read** | This whole page before starting --- the ordering matters |

## Flight controller waterproofing

First ensure that the FC fits within the 3D box before anything else.

1. Fill the bottom of the box with silicone sealant until it reaches the USB
   port hole.
2. *Carefully* slide the assembly in, with the Seeeduino facing the bottom
   of the box.
3. **Very important!** Insert a USB-C cable into the port. This keeps the
   sealant from flowing into the port, and the cable is a convenient point to
   hold the assembly by.
4. Add sealant along the three free edges to fill any gaps, until the sealant
   reaches the level of the top side of the PCB.
5. Let the silicone cure - because of the depth this takes about 12--24 h.

## ESC waterproofing
![The B-G431B-ESC1 assembly. ](/Fig/g431-power-stage.jpg){#fig-g431-power width="50%"}

The ESC is potted the same way as the flight controller: it sits in its own
3D-printed frame, which is then filled with **Silcoset** so only the wire exits
remain open. @fig-esc-potted shows the three pieces together - motor, bare
ESC, and the potted frame.

![The motor, the ESC and the potted frame. The dark block is the frame filled with Silcoset; the ESC drops into it before the fill so the board ends up fully encapsulated with only the phase and signal wires leaving.](/Fig/esc-potted.png){#fig-esc-potted width="65%"}

## Gearbox
By default the gearbox on the FAAV4 robot is **not waterproof at all**, and it
is normal for it to end up completely filled with water once submerged. Over
years of use the gearbox proved resistant to fresh water with the factory lubricant. If that is removed/cleaned, then use the right lubricant below. The best is to avoid opening the gearbox and cleaning the gears.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Use the right lubricant

A mix of **CorrosionX and white lithium grease**. 
Several dives have since been performed with the same gearbox that previously
corroded, and it now runs smoothly.
:::

Parts that rust: **sun gear, planet gears, ring gear, planet shafts.**
Parts that do not: screws, motor shaft, washers, body, circlip.

::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint

Flight controller and ESC fully cured and potted, static immersion test passed with no ingress. Robot cleaned with IPA after each immersion.
:::
